scale_003:n1.prompt:
You are helping me draft the first complete version of our employee handbook. Before starting, ask me for any of the following you don't already have: company legal name, state(s)/countries of operation, at-will employment status, current PTO policy details (accrual rates, carryover, holidays observed), remote/hybrid work policy specifics, equity plan basics (vesting schedule, plan name, whether we use a cap table tool), code of conduct expectations, benefits summary, and any existing policy documents or notes I can share as source material.

Once you have this information, draft complete handbook sections covering: Welcome/Company Overview, Employment Basics (at-will status, classification), Code of Conduct, Anti-Harassment/Equal Opportunity, PTO and Leave Policies, Remote/Hybrid Work Policy, Compensation and Equity Overview (plain-language explanation, not legal/tax advice), Benefits Overview, Workplace Safety, Technology/Data Use Policy, and Offboarding. Write in clear, plain language appropriate for employees, organized with headers and consistent formatting so it can be exported to a document or wiki page later.

Flag explicitly any section where you are inserting a placeholder because I haven't given you company-specific details (e.g., '[INSERT STATE-SPECIFIC LEAVE LAW LANGUAGE]'), and note anywhere you recommend I have an employment attorney review language before publishing, since this handbook will have legal implications.

When done, give me: (1) the full draft organized by section, (2) a list of open questions or missing inputs you need from me, and (3) a list of sections you flagged for legal review. Do not publish, distribute, or represent this draft as final policy — this is a draft for my review only.

scale_003:n2.prompt:
You are helping me customize our employee handbook policies (PTO, conduct, remote work, and equity) based on our company's actual practices. This is a drafting task only — a human must review and approve before anything becomes official.

First, ask me for any of the following you don't already have:
- Our company name, legal entity name, and state(s)/countries of operation
- Our PTO policy specifics (accrual rate, carryover rules, unlimited vs. fixed, sick leave, holidays)
- Remote/hybrid work rules (eligibility, expected hours, equipment stipend, expense reimbursement)
- Code of conduct expectations specific to us (dress code if any, anti-harassment reporting chain, disciplinary process)
- Equity plan details (vesting schedule, cliff, plan name, who is eligible, how grants are communicated)
- The base handbook template or existing draft I want you to customize (ask me to share the document or its location)

Using these inputs, draft customized policy language for each section (PTO, conduct, remote work, equity) that replaces generic placeholder text with our specifics. Keep tone and formatting consistent with the rest of the handbook. Flag clearly, in a comments or notes section, any spot where you had to make an assumption or where information I gave you was incomplete or ambiguous, so I can confirm it.

Produce the customized draft in a shared doc (e.g., Google Doc or the same format as the base template) along with a short summary checklist listing: which sections were customized, what assumptions were made, and what open questions remain for me to resolve.

When the draft and checklist are ready, stop for human sign-off — do not publish, distribute, or mark the handbook as final. Report back with a link to the draft, the checklist, and a list of any missing inputs you still need from me.

scale_003:n3.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the legal review step for our employee handbook before it can be published. This step requires a licensed attorney's explicit approval and I must not treat any AI output as legal sign-off.

Please do the following:
1. Ask me for: (a) the current draft of the employee handbook (file or link), (b) the list of jurisdictions/states/countries where we have employees, (c) the name/email of the outside employment attorney or law firm we use (or ask me if I need to find one), and (d) any prior legal review notes or deadlines.
2. Prepare a clear, organized review package: a summary of the handbook's sections (PTO, conduct, remote work, equity, etc.), a list of jurisdictions needing compliance checks, and a short cover note/email draft requesting the attorney's review, including a suggested deadline.
3. Draft the outbound email or message to the attorney, ready for me to send, including the handbook attached/linked and specific questions (e.g., "Please confirm compliance with employment law in [jurisdictions] and flag any required changes").
4. Set up a simple tracking checklist noting: date sent, attorney name, expected turnaround, and a placeholder for their feedback/approval status, since this is an async step — you should note that the result will land later and must be polled or checked back on rather than assumed complete.
5. Do NOT approve, sign, or mark the handbook as legally compliant yourself, and do not publish or apply any changes based on assumed approval.

When the review package and email draft are ready, report back with: the summary document, the draft email, the tracking checklist, and a clear note that this remains a human step — the attorney's actual sign-off is required and you should stop for human sign-off before any handbook changes are published.

scale_003:n4.prompt: You are helping me publish our finished employee handbook (policies, PTO, conduct, remote work, equity) as pages in {{vendor}}, our project-management/docs tool. Before starting, ask me for: (1) the finalized handbook content or file, (2) the {{vendor}} workspace/team name where it should live, and (3) the parent page or section it should be nested under. Using my configured credentials, prepare the handbook as one or more well-organized {{vendor}} pages: a top-level 'Employee Handbook' page with clearly named sub-pages for each major topic (Policies, PTO, Conduct, Remote Work, Equity), matching the structure and headings of the source content. Use the {{vendor}} API's page-creation capability to draft these pages in a staging/private area (not yet shared broadly), preserving formatting like headers, bullet lists, and tables where possible. Do not make the pages public, share them company-wide, or mark them final — this step requires my explicit approval before anything goes live. Once drafted, give me: a summary of the page structure created, direct links to each draft page, and a checklist confirming all five topic areas are present and accurately reflect the source content. Flag any content that seems incomplete, ambiguous, or that you had to reformat significantly. Then stop for human sign-off — do not publish, share, or notify employees until I confirm the drafts are approved and tell you to proceed with any further distribution.

scale_003:n5.prompt:
You are helping me finish the 'Employee handbook' process at the final step: sending the announcement email via Gmail. Before drafting, ask me for anything missing: (1) the link or location of the published handbook (e.g., shared drive or intranet URL), (2) the list of recipients or the team distribution list/group email to notify, (3) the effective date the handbook takes effect, (4) 3-5 key highlights or changes I want called out (e.g., new PTO policy, remote work, equity, conduct updates), and (5) the Gmail address/account I want the draft created under (use my configured credentials).

Once you have these, compose a clear, professional announcement email in Gmail as a DRAFT only (do not send it). The draft should include: a concise subject line referencing the employee handbook, a friendly opening, a summary of the key highlights I gave you, the handbook link, the effective date, and a closing line inviting questions or feedback. Address it to the recipients/list I specify.

Save this as a Gmail draft using my configured credentials — do not send, schedule, or share it further. Since sending requires my explicit approval before changes are applied, you must stop for human sign-off once the draft is ready.

When done, report back: the draft's subject line, the recipient list used, a copy of the full draft text for my review, and confirmation that it is saved as a draft in Gmail awaiting my approval to send.
